chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Abi Najran from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl who said:

We were in the hallway of Yahya ibn Khalid in Mecca, and there was Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) and Abu Yusuf. So Abu Yusuf stood up to him and squatted in front of him and said, 'O Abu al-Hasan, may I be sacrificed for you, does the one in Ihram shade himself?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'So does he shade by the wall and the carriage, and enter the house and the tent?' He said, 'Yes.' So he said, 'Yes.' So Abu Yusuf laughed as if mocking.

So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to him, 'O Abu Yusuf, indeed the Religion is not by analogy like your analogy and the analogy of your companions. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded in His Book regarding divorce and emphasized it with two witnesses, and He was not pleased with them except if they were two just men. And He commanded in His Book regarding marriage and left it without witnesses. So you have brought two witnesses in what Allah has voided, and you have voided two witnesses in what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has emphasized, and you have accepted the divorce of the insane and the intoxicated.'

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) performed Hajj, so he entered Ihram and did not shade himself, and entered the house and the tent, and shaded with the carriage and the wall. We did as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did. So he was silent.

key_terms.القياس: Analogy (qiyas, a method of legal reasoning)
key_terms.يُظَلِّل: To shade oneself (specifically covering the head/body from sun)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for shading oneself while in Ihram according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the Shia critique of Sunni analogical reasoning (Qiyas) by contrasting it with the explicit practice of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) demonstrates that the prohibition of shading in Ihram is specific to covering the head, as evidenced by the Prophet’s use of tents and mounts for shelter, thereby rejecting the extension of rulings through mere analogy.
